payload.name: Search emotion/appreciation statements for view questions
payload.description: Use when a question asks how a person views, regards, or thinks of something; before answering, also search for concrete emotion/appreciation expressions such as grateful, thankful, loves, or family.
content: When a question asks how someone views or regards something (e.g., 'what does X view Y as?'), do not rely only on queries containing abstract words like view, perception, or opinion; those words may be absent from stored memories.

Run supplementary searches combining the person with concrete emotion/appreciation/relationship terms (e.g., grateful, thankful, loves, 'part of the family') and with the target entity, and inspect event and preference memories for explicit attitudinal statements.

Before answering, require evidence that states the person's view or feeling explicitly; if retrieved evidence only shows related behaviors or plans (e.g., adopting, volunteering, activities), continue searching instead of inferring the view from behavior alone.

solves: Questions asking how someone views/regards something can be answered by explicit emotion/framing statements (e.g., grateful, part of the family) that are not retrieved by abstract terms like view or opinion; the agent wrongly inferred the view from behavioral evidence. This skill mandates searching for such expressions and requiring explicit attitudinal evidence before answering, applying to any person/entity view question, not to counts or period activities.
